scenarios.query:
Audit this docs parity scan:
```text
README: setup section says `docker compose up` — compose file deleted in March,
  replaced by `make dev`; badge links to CI that was migrated
API docs: document DELETE /v2/teams/{id} — endpoint removed two releases ago;
  new POST /v2/teams/{id}/archive undocumented
docstring: send_invoice(to, cc=None) — docs describe parameter `bcc` (never existed)
  and claim it raises InvoiceError; it actually returns an error result object
```
expected_behavior: Flags the broken README setup instructions (deleted compose file) as an onboarding regression
Flags the contradictory API docs: a documented endpoint that no longer exists and a new endpoint with no docs
Flags the docstring describing a nonexistent parameter and wrong error behavior as worse than no docs

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
new feature shipped last month: scheduled exports (cron jobs, a queue, an alert)
  - tutorial written (how to click through the UI)
  - no reference for the 6 new config keys
  - no runbook: on-call has no detect/diagnose/rollback steps (paged twice already)
ADRs: none for the new queue dependency (RabbitMQ added; no decision record)
```
expected_behavior: Flags the missing reference docs for the new config keys (a tutorial is not a substitute for reference)
Flags the missing runbook for the new operational surface, citing the on-call pages
Flags the missing ADR for the architecturally significant new dependency

scenarios.query:
Audit this repository. These are the raw files, not a pre-digested scan.

`README.md` (excerpt):
```markdown
## Install
    pip install acme-lib

## Quickstart
    from acme import Client
    c = Client(api_key="...")
    c.widgets.list(page=1)
```

`src/acme/widgets.py` (excerpt, current on disk):
```python
class Widgets:
    def list(self, cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = 50):
        """List widgets.

        Args:
            page: page number to fetch, 1-indexed.
        """
        ...
```
expected_behavior: Reads the actual source, not just a summary, and notices `Widgets.list` was changed to cursor-based pagination (`cursor`, `limit`) while its own docstring still documents a `page` parameter that no longer exists
Flags that the README's quickstart example (`c.widgets.list(page=1)`) calls the old, now-nonexistent parameter — the documented minimal example no longer runs against the current code
Treats this as both a docstring-accuracy defect and a runnable-example defect, not just one or the other

scenarios.query:
Audit this repository. These are the raw files, not a pre-digested scan.

`AGENTS.md` (repo root, unchanged by recent commits):
```markdown
## Build & test
    make build
    make test

## Layout
    scripts/deploy.sh handles releases; run it from repo root.
```

`git log --stat` (most recent commits, this repo):
```text
a1b2c3d  rename scripts/deploy.sh -> scripts/release.sh; update CI workflow
         to call scripts/release.sh
e4f5a6b  Makefile: `test` target removed, replaced by `just test` (justfile added)
```
expected_behavior: Notices the AGENTS.md-documented `scripts/deploy.sh` was renamed to `scripts/release.sh` in the actual commit history, and that the file itself was never updated to match
Notices `make test` no longer works (the target was removed in favor of `just test`) while AGENTS.md still tells an agent to run it

Flags the higher blast radius of this drift class: an agent following AGENTS.md literally will run a command that doesn't exist or point at a deleted script, not just a human who might notice and adapt

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
docs/guides/rate-limiting.md — doctest block:
  >>> client.set_rate_limit(rps=10)
  RateLimitConfig(requests_per_second=10)

src/client.py (current): `set_rate_limit` renamed to `configure_rate_limit`
in the last release; the doctest was not updated and is not run in CI.
```
expected_behavior: Flags that the doc's example calls a method (`set_rate_limit`) that no longer exists — the doctest would fail if it were ever run
Flags that the example is not wired into CI (no doctest runner), which is how it went stale unnoticed
Recommends the example be updated to the current API and run in CI so it can't rot silently again

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
CHANGELOG.md, most recent entry:
  ## 4.2.0
  ### Added
  - New `strict` option for the parser

Actual diff for 4.2.0 (per the release commit): also removed the deprecated
`Parser.legacy_mode()` method entirely — no entry for this in the changelog,
and no `### Removed` / `### Breaking` section for the release.
```
expected_behavior: Flags that a breaking removal (`Parser.legacy_mode()`) shipped in this release has no changelog entry at all — only the unrelated additive change was recorded
Flags the missing `Removed`/`Breaking` categorization for a release that actually contains one
Notes the consequence: a consumer scanning the changelog for breaking changes before upgrading would see nothing and be surprised

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
docs/architecture/diagram.png — a binary image, last modified 14 months ago,
showing three services: api, worker, and the (since-removed) legacy-sync
service. git history shows legacy-sync was deleted 6 months ago; no
corresponding diagram update. No source (Mermaid/PlantUML/etc.) exists for
this diagram — the PNG is the only copy.
```
expected_behavior: Flags the diagram as stale — it still depicts a service (legacy-sync) that was removed 6 months ago, actively misleading anyone using it to understand the current architecture
Flags that the diagram exists only as a binary image with no diffable source (Mermaid/PlantUML/etc.), which is part of why it silently went stale — there is no text diff to notice
Recommends both fixing the immediate staleness and converting the diagram to versioned text so future drift is diffable and reviewable

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
src/billing/invoice.py:
  # NOTE: totals are computed in the customer's local currency; the
  # dashboard converts to USD for display.
  def compute_total(items):
      return sum(i.amount_usd for i in items)   # changed to USD-only 3 commits ago

The comment was not updated when compute_total was changed to operate
directly in USD (amount_usd) rather than local currency.
```
expected_behavior: Flags that the comment describes behavior (`totals ... in the customer's local currency`) the code no longer has — `compute_total` now sums a USD field directly
Treats this as comment rot: the comment was left in place across the change that falsified it, rather than updated or removed
Notes the risk of a stale comment specifically here: a reader trusting the comment could misunderstand what currency the total is actually in

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
docs/internals/retry-budget.md — a genuinely thorough page on the new retry-budget
system (added last month: motivation, algorithm, config keys, examples).
Not linked from README.md, the docs index, mkdocs.yml nav, or any other page.
The only way to find it is to already know the exact filename.
```
expected_behavior: Flags that a well-written, substantive doc page is effectively invisible — not linked from the README, the docs index/nav, or anywhere else a reader would discover it
Distinguishes this from a content-quality problem: the page itself is fine, the defect is discoverability — findable only by already knowing the filename
Recommends linking it from the relevant index/nav rather than rewriting the content, since the content isn't the issue

scenarios.query:

```text
docs/tutorials/getting-started.md (last edited 2 years ago): "Step 3: run
`acme migrate --legacy` to set up your database."

`acme migrate --legacy` was removed 8 months ago (git log: "remove
```

Treats this as an orphaned/contradictory doc left in place after the feature it describes was removed, not merely 'outdated'
Wants the tutorial updated or removed/superseded, not left live and actively wrong

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
PR: switches the primary datastore's consistency model from strong
(synchronous replication) to eventual (async replication with a
convergence window), to cut write latency. Justification is a paragraph in
the PR description. No ADR exists for this repository's data-consistency
guarantees, before or after this change.
```
expected_behavior: Flags the absence of an ADR for an architecturally significant, surprising trade-off — switching consistency models changes what every caller can assume about read-after-write behavior

Notes that a PR-description paragraph is not a substitute for a durable decision record: the rationale, alternatives considered, and consequences need to be captured where future readers (and future changes) can find them, not buried in a merged PR's description
Does not treat this as adequately documented just because *some* justification text exists somewhere

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
docs/reference/api.md: complete, accurate reference for every public
endpoint — parameters, types, response shapes, error codes. No how-to
guide anywhere in the docs for the single most common task (batch-importing
records), despite it being the #1 support request per the linked ticket
tag.
```
expected_behavior: Flags the missing how-to guide for the most common task (batch import) as a real gap even though the reference docs are complete and accurate — reference answers 'what are the parameters,' not 'how do I accomplish X'
Recognizes this as a Diátaxis-mode gap (missing the task-oriented how-to quadrant), not a parity or accuracy problem — the existing docs are correct as far as they go
Grounds the priority in the cited evidence (the #1 support request), not just asserting the gap in the abstract

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
Repo: an internal CLI used by 2 people on the same team, no external
consumers, no support rotation. Docs: a single README with install +
usage, no ADRs, no runbook, no changelog. Team has discussed this and
decided the overhead of fuller documentation isn't worth it for a
two-person internal tool.
```
expected_behavior: Notes what's present (a working README with install/usage) rather than opening with what's absent

Recognizes that the right documentation investment level for a two-person internal tool with no external consumers and no support rotation is a team/product judgment call, not a fixed bar this lens should impose uniformly — routes the question rather than mandating ADRs/runbooks/changelog the team has deliberately decided against
Does not block or demand parity with a public-facing project's documentation bar

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
Docstrings are hand-maintained across 40 modules; coverage is good but three
have drifted this quarter (caught by this audit). Team is debating whether
to adopt an API-doc generator (e.g. an OpenAPI/docstring-extraction
pipeline) that would auto-sync docs from signatures, estimated at 3
```

expected_behavior: Flags the three modules with drifted docstrings that this audit actually found, with specifics

Recognizes that whether to invest in doc-generation tooling versus hand-maintained docs with better review discipline is a build-vs-buy/tooling-investment call for engineering leadership, not something this audit's checklist should mandate one way or the other
Surfaces the trade-off (drift risk vs. tooling cost) rather than prescribing the generator as the fix

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
CHANGELOG.md, latest entry: "## 3.1.0 -- No breaking changes."

Actual diff for 3.1.0: removes the `Config.from_env()` classmethod (public
```

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
docs/runbooks/nightly-reconciliation.md: "Last reviewed: this quarter.
Detect: check the #ops-alerts channel. Diagnose: see the dashboard.
Rollback: re-run the job with --dry-run=false."

The `nightly-reconciliation` job itself was deleted 4 months ago (replaced
by an event-driven reconciliation stream with no equivalent runbook). The
"last reviewed" stamp was applied by a doc-freshness bot that only checks
```

expected_behavior: Does not accept the 'last reviewed: this quarter' stamp as evidence the runbook is current — checks whether the job it describes still exists
Flags that the underlying job was deleted 4 months ago and has no equivalent runbook for its event-driven replacement — on-call has nothing usable for the system that actually runs today
Flags the freshness-stamping mechanism itself as misleading: a bot that only checks edit recency, not whether the described system still exists, produces false confidence

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
Release 5.0.0: removes `Client.legacy_auth()`.
CHANGELOG.md: "## 5.0.0 -- ### Breaking: removed `Client.legacy_auth()`,
use `Client.authenticate()` (deprecated with a warning since 4.2.0)."

current and accurate.
No ADR needed (routine deprecation-completion, not a new architectural
```

expected_behavior: Reports no substantive findings — the removal is correctly categorized as Breaking in the changelog with a pointer to the replacement, the reference docs were updated in the same release, and the quickstart still runs
Does not demand an ADR for a routine, already-signaled deprecation completion — recognizes this isn't a new architecturally significant decision
Does not manufacture additional documentation requirements on an already-consistent release

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
Internal data-pipeline repo, 4 contributors, no external users. Docs: a
README (setup + architecture overview, accurate and current), inline
docstrings on all public functions (parity-checked, accurate), and a
one-page runbook for the one on-call-relevant job. No separate tutorial/
how-to docs, no ADR directory, no CHANGELOG (version is just the deploy
timestamp). The team has stated this level is deliberate for an internal,
low-churn pipeline with a stable, known audience.
```
expected_behavior: Reports no substantive findings — README, docstrings, and the one operationally relevant runbook are all present, accurate, and current
Does not demand a CHANGELOG, ADR directory, or tutorial/how-to docs the team has deliberately decided are unnecessary overhead for this repo's actual audience and change pattern
Recognizes documentation health as parity and accuracy for what exists, not a fixed artifact checklist every repo must carry regardless of shape or audience

scenarios.query:
Audit this scan:
```text
The only artifacts available for this repository are source-metrics
counters: 41 Python modules, average cyclomatic complexity 6.2, no
duplicate-code clusters detected, test coverage 87%. No README, docstring,
changelog, ADR, runbook, or any other documentation artifact was included
in this scan.
```
expected_behavior: States plainly that no documentation artifacts were provided to audit — this scan contains only source-complexity metrics, nothing this lens's checklist applies to — rather than reporting a bare "No findings" that would read as a documentation check that ran and passed
Does not infer or assume documentation health (or its absence) from complexity/coverage metrics alone, since those say nothing about docs
Matches the lens's own reviewer-discipline distinction between 'checked and clean' and 'not applicable to this scan'
